AlreadyInitialized().details: Emitted when attempting to initialize an already initialized or locked contract.

Initialized(uint8).details: Triggered when the contract has been initialized or reinitialized.

allowSpmlNode(address).details: The broker lists a payee by itself the first time the spml reports      it, so the list is not an independent check on the signer: it only      records which addresses this provider has been asked to pay. A listed      address is still paid only against a signer's voucher.

optInSpml().details: Consent to enter only, and permanent: the provider key is a hot key in      the broker, so it cannot withdraw the consent, choose the signer or      leave spml mode (those would let its holder redirect or drain the pool).      After a clear the owner can re-enter the provider without a second opt-in.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

previewSettlementResults((address,addres.details: WARNING: If the same user appears multiple times in the batch,      only the first occurrence will show accurate preview results.      Subsequent occurrences will use stale balance/nonce values since      this is a view function that cannot simulate state changes.      For accurate preview of batches with duplicate users, call this      function separately for each unique user.

params.settlements: Array of settlement data to preview

returns.failedUsers: Array of user addresses that failed validation
returns.failureReasons: Array of failure reasons corresponding to failedUsers
returns.partialAmounts: Array of unsettled amounts corresponding to partialUsers
returns.partialUsers: Array of user addresses with insufficient balance

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions anymore. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby removing any functionality that is only available to the owner.

revokeSpmlSigner(address,address).details: Vouchers they signed and nodes have not redeemed stop working; the      replacement signer re-issues them (vouchers are cumulative, so nothing      is lost while the spml's ledger is intact). With no replacement the      provider leaves spml mode and the pool stays locked for SIGNER_GRACE      as on a clear, so a revoke cannot be used as an exit without notice.      A replacement for a provider that is already out of spml mode (cleared,      old signer still in its grace) is an entry: it needs the provider's      opt-in like setSpmlSigner (SpmlNotOptedIn); zero always works.

params.replacement: The new signer (never the provider itself), or zero to leave spml mode

setSpmlSigner(address,address).details: Trust model: the pool is controlled by whoever signs vouchers. Whether a      key really is the spml verifier's (derived inside its attested TEE)      cannot be checked on-chain, so only the owner names the signer, takes a      provider out of spml mode, and releases a pool. A provider key (a hot      key in the broker) can do none of these; it can only agree to enter      spml mode (optInSpml) and list payees.      A signer that was in use before a pool withdrawal, or that was revoked,      cannot be set again (SpmlSignerRetired): the vouchers it already signed      would otherwise draw on deposits made after the withdrawal.      Consent: the owner can take a provider into spml mode only after that      provider called optInSpml() (SpmlNotOptedIn otherwise). Rotating the      signer of a provider already in spml mode needs nothing from it.

params.provider: The provider whose settlements the signer pays out
params.signer: The spml verifier's secp256k1 address (never zero, never the provider itself)

settleFeesWithTEE((address,address,uint2.details: Status codes: 0=SUCCESS, 1=PARTIAL_SETTLEMENT, 2=PROVIDER_MISMATCH, 3=NO_TEE_SIGNER, 4=INVALID_NONCE, 5=INVALID_SIGNATUREStatuses array has same length as input, with statuses[i] corresponding to settlements[i]All settlement details are emitted via TEESettlementResult events

params.settlements: Array of settlement data to process

returns.statuses: Array of settlement statuses (uint8), preserving one-to-one correspondence with input

transferOwnership(address).details: Transfers ownership of the contract to a new account (`newOwner`). Can only be called by the current owner.

allowSpmlNode(address).notice: Add a payee address to the calling provider's pool. claim() pays         only listed nodes (the signer's own cut is governed by the cap         instead). Listing is permanent: being unable to de-list means the         provider cannot void a node's vouchers.

claim(address,address,uint256,uint64,byt.notice: Redeem a cumulative PayoutVoucher signed by the provider's spml signer.         Anyone may submit; funds always go to the voucher's node address.         Replays are inert: cumulative must strictly exceed what the node has         already withdrawn, and only the delta is paid. The voucher binds the         provider, so two providers sharing one signer cannot pay each other's         vouchers out of their own pool.

clearSpmlSigner(address).notice: Take a provider out of spml mode: settlements go back to the         provider wallet from the next round. The current signer's in-flight         vouchers stay claimable for SIGNER_GRACE; after that the owner can         return what is left in the pool (withdrawSpmlPool).

isSpmlOptedIn(address).notice: True if the provider called optInSpml().

isSpmlSignerRetired(address,address).notice: True if setSpmlSigner would refuse this signer for this provider as retired         (SpmlSignerRetired). The provider's own address is refused too, but is not retired.

optInSpml().notice: The calling provider agrees to be put in spml mode, where its settled         fees go to a pool paid out by the spml's vouchers instead of to its         wallet. Without this the owner cannot take it into spml mode.

previewSettlementResults((address,addres.notice: Preview settlement results for a batch of settlements without state changes

revokeSpmlSigner(address,address).notice: Emergency stop for a leaked or misbehaving signer: the current signer         and the rotated-out one stop being honored in this block, with no         grace, and neither can be set for this provider again.

setSpmlSigner(address,address).notice: Register or rotate a provider's spml voucher signer. A non-zero         signer switches the provider's settlements into spml-pool mode:         settled funds accumulate in the pool and GPUs withdraw them via         claim() with an EIP-712 PayoutVoucher signed by this signer.         On rotation the previous signer's in-flight vouchers stay claimable         for SIGNER_GRACE.

setSpmlVerifierCutCap(uint256).notice: Cap (in basis points of the provider's cumulative pool deposits) on the         cumulative amount the spml signer may claim for itself as its cut.

settleFeesWithTEE((address,address,uint2.notice: Settle fees with TEE-signed settlement data

spmlVerifierPaidOf(address).notice: Cumulative amount the verifier has claimed as its own cut from this         provider's pool, across signer rotations (what the cut cap is checked against).

withdrawSpmlPool(address).notice: Return what is left in a provider's pool to that provider, once it         has left spml mode and SIGNER_GRACE has passed. Owner-only: the         remainder is fees no voucher attributed or vouchers nobody redeemed,         i.e. node earnings the spml can no longer pay out (lost ledger,         retired verifier). The owner confirms that off-chain before releasing         it; the funds can only go to the provider.
